!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: bioinfo +40%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months — queried directly, PubMed returns zero *Nucleic Acids Research* research articles dated 2025-12, and zero *Bioinformatics* in 2024-04, 2025-01, 2025-04 and 2026-03. Those holes are in the source and are reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest, so a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nucleic Acids Res 255, Nature 85, JAMA 79, Science 77, Bioinformatics 48, Lancet 41.

## 3. The evidence that moved it


!!! note "Written 2026-08-26, in arrears"
    2024 was added to the corpus nineteen months after the practice started,
    to test whether its "first appearance" claims survived a lower floor. None
    of them did. These twelve briefings are therefore written backwards, by
    someone who already knows what 2025 and 2026 did, and that is the opposite
    of the position the monthly practice is supposed to simulate. Read them as
    a baseline for the threads, not as a record of what was visible at the time.
    2024 was also read thread-first rather than exhaustively, so its card counts
    are a floor and are **not** comparable with 2025 and 2026 month totals.

**The agent era starts here, thirteen months before this corpus said it did.**
[38799228](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38799228/) (*Nat Mach Intell*) gives a large language model chemistry tools
and has it plan and execute syntheses. Until today the corpus dated the first
LLM-agent paper to ESCARGOT on 4 February 2025 and built a diffusion-lag
argument on it. That argument is void. The tool-using agent is in a tracked
journal in January 2024, and [38341654](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38341654/) (GeneGPT) follows in February.

**AlphaFold's own limits, stated in its own field's methods journal.**
[38036854](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38036854/) (*Nat Methods*): AlphaFold predictions are valuable hypotheses
that accelerate but **do not replace** experimental structure determination.
The most successful predictive model in biology publishes its own ceiling in
January 2024. Alongside it, [38082179](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38082179/) reports that macroscopic
resting-state brain dynamics are best described by *linear* models — a
simple-beats-complex title in the same month. The corpus previously dated that
genre to mid-2025.

**Two neural-immune mechanisms, in the two highest-tier venues.**
[38134932](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38134932/) (*Cell*): sensory neurons promote immune homeostasis in the
lung. [37947393](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37947393/): gliomas hijack adaptive plasticity to strengthen
neuron-tumour synapses. [38085267](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38085267/) adds commensal bacteria driving type I
interferon to maintain tolerance. The thread this corpus scores as its
healthiest is already running on all three of its arms — neural, microbial,
lymphoid — in the first month of the window.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[38071995](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38071995/): the FDA opens an investigation into secondary lymphomas after
CAR-T. The platform's safety case is reopened by a regulator rather than by a
trial, which is the earliest form this kind of refutation takes and the one
literature-only surveillance is worst at seeing. [37874957](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37874957/) adds that
recent bendamustine before apheresis degrades CAR-T outcomes — the product's
efficacy is contingent on prior therapy in a way the label did not anticipate.

[38296595](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38296595/) (*JITC*): **no** detrimental association between antibiotic use
and checkpoint inhibitor therapy, in a cohort assembled to find one. A widely
repeated microbiome-adjacent clinical claim fails to replicate, and it fails in
the same month the mechanistic microbiome papers above are being published.

### (b) Method credibility

[38150261](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38150261/) (*JAMA*): a large language model reproduces affiliation bias
when reviewing abstracts. The audit of machine judgement begins in the same
months as its adoption, not after it — a pattern that holds for every AI
modality in this corpus once the window is wide enough to see it.

[38172966](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38172966/) benchmarks differential-abundance methods for finding
condition-specific cells across multi-sample single-cell datasets.
